questions.question: Which Norse god carried a mighty hammer called Mjölnir?
questions.explanation: Thursday is named after Thor, which makes it Thor's day.

questions.question: Which Greek god ruled the sea?
questions.explanation: Poseidon carried a trident, a spear with three prongs, and could stir up storms and earthquakes.

questions.question: What was the name of King Arthur's famous sword?
questions.explanation: In many tellings it was given to Arthur by the Lady of the Lake.

questions.question: What did Icarus's father use to make wings for them both?
questions.explanation: Icarus flew too close to the Sun, the wax melted, and he fell into the sea.

questions.question: How did the Greek soldiers finally get inside the city of Troy?
questions.explanation: That is why a sneaky trick, or a harmful computer program disguised as something harmless, is called a Trojan horse.

questions.question: Which Greek hero went into the labyrinth to face the Minotaur?
questions.explanation: Princess Ariadne gave him a ball of thread so he could find his way back out.

questions.question: In Greek myths, what was the monster Medusa's hair made of?
questions.explanation: Anyone who looked straight at Medusa was turned to stone.

questions.question: In which forest did Robin Hood and his Merry Men hide?
questions.explanation: Sherwood's giant Major Oak is said to have been the outlaws' hideout.

questions.question: Which hero had to complete twelve impossible tasks, called labours?
questions.explanation: Hercules is the Roman name; the Greeks called him Heracles.

questions.question: What shape was the table where King Arthur's knights sat?
questions.explanation: A round table has no head, so no knight could claim the most important seat.

questions.question: In Greek myth, what was left inside after Pandora let all the troubles out into the world?
questions.explanation: All the bad things flew out, but Hope stayed behind.

questions.question: Which trickster god in Norse myths could change his shape?
questions.explanation: Loki could turn himself into all sorts of creatures, from a salmon to a fly.

questions.question: Which Greek hero led the Argonauts on their quest for the Golden Fleece?
questions.explanation: His crew were called the Argonauts because their ship was named the Argo.

questions.question: In Egyptian myths, which god had the head of a jackal?
questions.explanation: Anubis watched over the dead and was the god of making mummies.

questions.question: The ancient Egyptian god Ra was the god of what?
questions.explanation: The Egyptians pictured Ra sailing across the sky in a boat every day.

questions.question: Which Greek goddess sprang fully grown from the head of Zeus?
questions.explanation: Her sacred bird, the owl, is still a symbol of wisdom today.

questions.question: Who was the Roman version of Hermes, the messenger of the Greek gods?
questions.explanation: Mercury, the speediest planet, is named after the speedy messenger god.

questions.question: Who was King Arthur's queen?
questions.explanation: Her name comes from the Welsh Gwenhwyfar.

questions.question: Which of Robin Hood's men was jokingly named for being very big?
questions.explanation: In a famous ballad, he first meets Robin by beating him in a quarterstaff fight on a narrow bridge.

questions.question: Whose was the face that launched a thousand ships?
questions.explanation: The famous line comes from Christopher Marlowe's play Doctor Faustus.

questions.question: Who was the ferryman who carried the souls of the dead into the Greek underworld?
questions.explanation: The Greeks sometimes buried their dead with a coin to pay his fare.

questions.question: Which Greek hero blinded the Cyclops Polyphemus?
questions.explanation: He had told the Cyclops his name was Nobody, so when Polyphemus cried that Nobody was hurting him, no one came to help.

questions.question: In legend, to which island was King Arthur carried after his last battle?
questions.explanation: In 1191 the monks of Glastonbury claimed to have found Arthur's grave.

questions.question: Which Titan was punished by Zeus for giving fire to humans?
questions.explanation: Atlas, another Titan, got a different punishment: holding up the sky.

questions.question: Which musician went down to the underworld to bring back his wife, Eurydice?
questions.explanation: He was told not to look back until they reached daylight, and he could not resist.

questions.question: In Egyptian myth, which god was killed by his brother Set and brought back to life by Isis?
questions.explanation: Osiris became king of the underworld and is often painted with green skin.

questions.question: What was the name of Odin's eight-legged horse?
questions.explanation: Sleipnir's mother was, of all people, the shape-shifting god Loki.

questions.question: In Norse myth, which god is killed by the wolf Fenrir at Ragnarök?
questions.explanation: Tyr had lost a hand to Fenrir when the gods tricked the wolf into being tied up.

questions.question: In Egyptian belief, what was a dead person's heart weighed against in the afterlife?
questions.explanation: The feather belonged to Ma'at, the goddess of truth and justice.

questions.question: Which Norse god guards Bifröst, the rainbow bridge to Asgard?
questions.explanation: He will blow his horn, Gjallarhorn, to warn the gods that Ragnarök has begun.
